searchText: Hey <@388610194608750595>, I’m trying to reach the same conclusion as <@994843128961966110> during your previous conversation which I’ve replied to above. We’re building a (—fee recipient) smoothing pool for solo stakers and worried about the same type of exploit where a user could steal from the pool a large MEV payout by writing custom script to change their fee recipient based on the size of the bid received. Is this a valid concern? I’ve been actively monitoring RocketPool’s smoothing pool and have not seen any occurrences of this type and there have been plenty of large deposits to that pool. yeah sorry, ill go add some docs 🙂 and also will debug the engine api proxying -- i would guess prysm is doing something a bit differently as i have only tested w/ lighthouse is this a slow reponse or something else? it looks like there is a "serialization error" at the end of your logs there's a mev boost <-> FB goerli relay pair in there. Nimbus's serialization error is just how Nimbus sees mev-boost's 502 "no payload received from relay" i think sometimes that call will fail in mev-boost and it would simply take a retry for the call to succeed
